title: Quarter conditioning raises a 60-day dip-count tail fraction from 0.0010 to 0.25 for KIC 8462852
abstract: We test a count statistic for known KIC 8462852 dips in Kepler DR25 data. Five events pass a 1 percent local aperture-flux threshold and persistence cuts. Four fall in a 60-day interval. In 100,000 trials, uniform eligible exposure times with a two-day separation cut give a tail fraction of 0.000980. Fixing the event count in each quarter gives 0.24955. Both models scan all start times. A five-day separation test retains the difference. Higher flux thresholds give weaker uniform-time evidence. The corrected flux product gives similar counts but shares photons. All accepted 2 and 5 percent Gaussian dips are recovered in quiet-patch tests. These checks cover one synthetic shape and do not establish survey completeness. The result shows that the timing evidence depends on the assumed rate model. The late dip group is known. Target and scale choices use prior knowledge, so the fractions are not discovery false-alarm probabilities. No new event, planet, dust cause, or independent confirmation is established. Code, hashes, event times, aggregate simulations, audits and retrieval steps are included.
